questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

"__I'm afraid I must left now__," said the guest after the inaugural function was over.

options.text: I'm afraid I can left now
I'm afraid I has to be leaving now
I'm afraid I must leave now

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'I'm afraid I must leave now'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, we need to use bare infinitive **'leave'** instead of the past form** 'left'.**
 
• Modals__ are always followed by __bare infinitives.__ 
 __
 
• I can go__ there myself. 
 
 
 
• Infinitives are the base form of the verb used in conjugation with 'to'.
 
• When they are used without 'to', they are called 'bare infinitives'. 

**Hence, the correct sentence is** -* "__I'm afraid I must **leave** now__," said the guest after the inaugural function was over.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Even Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Even Sharat tried his best.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• As we have two sentences here we need a **conjunction** to connect both these sentence.
 
• **Even **is an **adverb** we have to replace it with a conjunction to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• As one sentence is positive and another is negative, so we need to use contradictory conjunction.
 
• **Although **is one such type of conjunction and will make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• We can also use '**Even though**'. 

**The correct sentence will be **- ***Although** Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt. OR** Even though** Sharat tried his best, he could not clear all the examination papers in one attempt.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence**.

His mother gave him a note for his teacher.

options.text: He was given a note for his teacher by his mother.
He is given a note for his teacher by his mother.
His teacher was given a note for his mother.
He had been given a note for his teacher by his mother

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**He was given a note for his teacher by his mother.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in the past indefinite tense. 
 
• The structure is Subject + V2 + Object.
 
• Such sentences are converted into passive in the following way:
 
• **Object + was/were+ V3 + by + subject.**
 
• Here, there are two objects - 'a note' and 'him'.
 
• 'A note' is the direct object and 'him' is the indirect object. 
 
• The sentence will start with the direct object.

This rule is followed by only option 1, so this is the correct choice.

questions.question: If it was a Sunday on 1 January 2017, what was the day of the week on 31 December 2017?
questions.solution:
Code for the days:

 
 

 
 
Code of the day

 
 
 
Day

 
 
 

 
 
0

 
 
 
Sunday

 
 
 

 
 
1

 
 
 
Monday

 
 
 

 
 
2

 
 
 
Tuesday

 
 
 

 
 
3

 
 
 
Wednesday

 
 
 

 
 
4

 
 
 
Thursday

 
 
 

 
 
5

 
 
 
Friday

 
 
 

 
 
6

 
 
 
Saturday

 
 
 

 

Given,

1 January 2017 is Sunday.

1 January 2017 (Sunday) + **364 days** (Because 2017 is not a leap year) = 31 December 2017.

**364 Days** = **0 odd days**.

So, 1 January 2017 (Sunday) + 364 days (0 odd days) = Sunday.

Therefore, 31 December 2017 = Sunday.

hence, the correct answer is "Sunday".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Year - One year has 365 days or 366 days on this basis the year is divided into two parts:

 
• Normal year - It has 365 days.
 
• Leap year - It has 366 days and is completely divisible by 4.

Century leap year - The year which is exactly divisible by 400. Example - 1200, 1600, 2000 etc.

Counting of Odd days

Ordinary Year: 365 days (52 weeks + 1 days)

= 1 Odd days

Leap Year: 366 days (52 weeks + 2 days)

= 2 Odd days

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

35 + 7 - 5 × 2 ÷ 25 = 20
questions.solution:

= 5 – 10 +25

= 30 - 10

= 20

Hence, the correct answer is '+ and ÷'.

Hence, the correct answer is 415.

questions.question: A shopkeeper normally allows a discount of 10% on the marked price of each article. During a sale season, he decides to give two more discounts, the first being at a rate of 50% of the original and the second at a rate of 40% of the first. What is the percentage rate of the equivalent single discount (correct up to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount percent on the marked price = 10%

Discount percent in the first case = 50% of 10 

Discount percent in the second case = 40% of the first case

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be Rs 100

⇒ Discount = 10% = 1/10 = (10 - 1)/10 = 9/10

S.P = 9/10 × 100 = 90

Now, Discount percent in the first case = 50% of 10 

⇒ 50/100 × 10 = 5%

And, Discount percent in the second case = 40% of the first case

⇒ 40/100 × 5 = 2%

Now the selling price in season is, 

⇒ 90 × (100 - 5)/100 × (100 - 2)/100

⇒ 90 × 95/100 × 98/100 

⇒ 83.79

Hence the actual discount is, 

⇒ 100 - 83.79 = 16.21

**∴ The percentage rate of the equivalent single discount 16.21%**

• Such a system of farming is practised only in that region of the country where the source of water is from underground or surface water bodies like rivers, tanks and lakes are sufficient throughout the year.

**dry farming**

 
• Dry agriculture is the cultivation done in dry and semi-dry areas where the average annual rainfall is about 75 cm.
 
• Dryland farming or rainfed farming is the technique of doing agriculture without irrigation.
 
• Crops are grown without irrigation by accumulating the limited moisture available under them.
 
• Due to the lack of rainfall, constant efforts are made to maintain and increase the moisture content of the soil.
 
• Features of dry agriculture are that it is cultivated in those areas where there is a lack of moisture for about 8 months in a year.

**mixed farming**

 
• **Mixed farming **is an agricultural system in which a farmer conducts different **agricultural practices, such as cash crops and livestock, together.** 
 
• The aim is to increase income through different sources and to complement land and labour demands across the year. 
 
• In an ideal case, the ratio of enterprise **Crops to livestock should be ~ 50%-50%.**
